title: LELA: an LLM-based Entity Linking Approach with Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation

While this body of work primarily targets document and passage retrieval, we demonstrate that pointwise LLM-based reranking, followed by reasoning-driven selection, can be effectively adapted to the entity linking setting without task-specific fine-tuning. Let the KB ℰ \mathcal{E} be a set of entities, each with a textual description. Given a mention m m in a text S S , the goal of entity linking is to find the entity e ∈ ℰ {e\in\mathcal{E}} that m m refers to in the context of S S , or, optionally, return a special entity e none e_{\text{none}} , which indicates that no entity is relevant. LELA uses a three-stage coarse-to-fine pipeline, as illustrated in Figure 2 : Candidate entities are first generated Sevgili et al. ( 2022 ); Wu et al. ( 2020 ) , then ranked, and then selected. Beyond the text, mention, and KB, LELA requires only a parameter k ∈ ℕ + k\in\mathbb{N}^{+} as input. The goal of the candidate generation step is to identify the entities C m ⊆ ℰ {C_{m}\subseteq\mathcal{E}} that could potentially be relevant to m m .
